title: Edit a media-club paragraph for controlled sentence variety
instructions: A school media club planned an audio archive of the old riverside market. Use only these verified notes when editing: the club interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday; the front room faced a bus stop, and traffic obscured parts of two recordings; the next session moved to a back room; each interviewer tested a microphone before recording; the later recordings were clearer; the club kept a separate file containing each speaker's name and interview date. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which revision turns the fragment ‘Interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday’ into a complete sentence without changing the fact?

options.text: The club interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday.
Although interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday.
Interviewing six former traders on its first Saturday.
Which interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday.

choice_rationales.A: The revision supplies the subject ‘the club’ and a complete finite verb.
choice_rationales.B: ‘Although’ creates a dependent opening without an independent clause.
choice_rationales.C: The -ing group does not supply a complete finite verb for the sentence.
choice_rationales.D: The relative word ‘which’ makes the clause dependent and leaves its referent unstated.

parts.hint: Find a version with an explicit subject and a finite verb that can stand alone.
parts.correct_explanation: A complete independent clause identifies who performed the recorded action.

parts.prompt: Which sentence best combines the location and recording problem to express their causal relationship?

options.text: The front room faced a bus stop, traffic obscured parts of two recordings.
Because the front room faced a bus stop, traffic obscured parts of two recordings.
Because the front room faced a bus stop, so traffic obscured parts of two recordings.
The front room faced a bus stop, although traffic therefore obscured parts of two recordings.

choice_rationales.A: A comma alone does not create a valid boundary between the two independent clauses.
choice_rationales.B: The dependent opening makes the location the cause and attaches it to a complete result clause.
choice_rationales.C: ‘Because’ and ‘so’ duplicate the same causal link in this structure.
choice_rationales.D: ‘Although’ signals concession while ‘therefore’ signals consequence, so the relationship is contradictory.

parts.hint: Choose one grammatical structure that makes the first fact explain the second.
parts.correct_explanation: A single subordinating marker expresses cause clearly and avoids both a comma splice and a doubled connector.

parts.prompt: Which revision completes the dependent fragment ‘Because traffic had obscured parts of two interviews’ and preserves the sequence in the notes?

options.text: Because traffic had obscured parts of two interviews.
Traffic having obscured parts of two interviews.
Because traffic had obscured parts of two interviews, the club moved its next session to a back room.
Because traffic had obscured parts of two interviews, and the next session in a back room.

choice_rationales.A: The ‘because’ clause still leaves the reader waiting for its result.
choice_rationales.B: The participial group has no independent clause or complete finite verb.
choice_rationales.C: The main clause completes the causal relationship and follows the recorded order of events.
choice_rationales.D: The words after the comma do not form a complete independent clause.

parts.hint: The ‘because’ clause needs a complete main clause stating what happened next.
parts.correct_explanation: Subordination creates variety safely only when the dependent idea is attached to a complete independent clause.

parts.prompt: Which revision corrects agreement and removes unclear pronoun reference from ‘Each of the interviewers were asked to test their microphone, and this improved them’ while staying within the notes?

options.text: Each of the interviewers were asked to test a microphone, and this improved them.
Each interviewer was asked to test a microphone before recording; after the move and sound checks, the later recordings were clearer.
Each interviewer was asked to test them, and it made this clearer.
Each of the interviewers have tested a microphone, proving that it improved every interview.

choice_rationales.A: The singular subject ‘each’ still disagrees with ‘were’, while ‘this’ and ‘them’ remain unclear.
choice_rationales.B: ‘Each’ agrees with ‘was’, and the second clause names both the preceding changes and the observed recordings.
choice_rationales.C: Agreement is repaired, but the pronouns have no unmistakable referents.
choice_rationales.D: ‘Each’ does not agree with ‘have’, and the sentence claims proof and a universal result absent from the notes.

parts.hint: Find the head subject for agreement, then make every pronoun point to one named referent.
parts.correct_explanation: Sentence combining must preserve subject–verb agreement and replace ambiguous pointers with the exact action and result.

parts.prompt: Which THREE sentences are complete and use their structures to show a clear relationship or emphasis?

options.text: When the first session ended, the club checked the audio.
Although the front room faced the bus stop.
The traffic was loud, it obscured parts of two recordings.
The club moved to the back room, where each interviewer tested a microphone.
Each of the interviewers were responsible for a sound check.
The team changed its routine. The later recordings were clearer.

choice_rationales.A: The time clause is attached to a complete main clause and establishes sequence.
choice_rationales.B: The concessive clause is a fragment because it lacks a main clause.
choice_rationales.C: The two independent clauses form a comma splice.
choice_rationales.D: The relative clause adds a related action to a complete main clause.
choice_rationales.E: The singular head subject ‘each’ requires ‘was’, not ‘were’.
choice_rationales.F: Both sentences are complete, and the short result sentence receives appropriate emphasis.

parts.hint: Check completeness and agreement before considering whether the pattern creates useful emphasis.
parts.correct_explanation: Controlled variety can use a time clause, a relative clause or a deliberately short result sentence without sacrificing grammatical completeness.

parts.prompt: Which revised paragraph uses sentence variety with the strongest control throughout?

options.text: Planning an archive of the market. The club interviewed traders, the room faced a bus stop. Because the traffic. Moving rooms and testing them.

The media club planned an audio archive of the old riverside market and interviewed six former traders on its first Saturday. Because the front room faced a bus stop, traffic obscured parts of two recordings. The club therefore moved its next session to a back room, where each interviewer tested a microphone before recording. The later recordings were clearer. To preserve context, the club also kept a separate file with each speaker's name and interview date.
The club planned an archive, and it interviewed traders, and it used a room, and the room was noisy, and it moved, and it tested microphones, and the recordings improved.
Although the club interviewed six traders. Traffic obscured two recordings, therefore the next session moved itself, which made them clearer because it tested every microphone.

choice_rationales.A: Fragments and a comma splice prevent the sequence from forming complete, controlled sentences.
choice_rationales.B: Coordination, subordination, a relative clause, a short result and a purpose opening each serve a distinct relationship while agreement and reference remain clear.
choice_rationales.C: Repeated coordination overloads one sentence and leaves every idea at the same level of emphasis.
choice_rationales.D: The opening is a fragment, the session cannot move itself, and the pronouns and causal claim are unclear.

parts.hint: Choose the paragraph whose varied patterns reveal cause, attached detail, result and purpose without grammar or reference errors.
parts.correct_explanation: Purposeful variety follows the paragraph's logic: sentence structures change because the relationships and emphasis change.
